summary: Add many-to-many alert tags, assignment/removal endpoints, tag filtering, and response tags.
adjacent_dependencies: AlertService.API.Tests test doubles and service interface consumers
constraints: Keep controller -> service -> repository layering and async behavior.
Deduplicate submitted tags case-insensitively before enforcing the maximum of 10 unique tags per alert.
Validate each tag at the trust boundary for 1-30 characters.
Preserve existing pagination, filters, sorting, error middleware, and response mapping conventions.
Full dotnet test includes unrelated ALERT-411/ALERT-412 expectations; use focused filters.
Local migration validation may encounter an existing Tags database object.
coverage_goals: POST assigns multiple tags and deduplicates case-insensitively.
POST rejects tags outside 1-30 characters and more than 10 unique tags.
DELETE removes assignments and returns 404 for a missing alert or assignment.
GET tag filtering composes with active, severity, date range, and title search filters.
Alert responses include tags and persistence uses the many-to-many join table.
missing_facts: Exact new tag request/entity/configuration file naming convention is not yet established.
Required AlertResponse tag representation is unspecified.
Whether stored tag casing preserves first submission casing is unspecified.
Whether reassigning an already-assigned tag is idempotent or returns a conflict is unspecified.
Whether the ten-tag limit is evaluated after unique normalized tags is an assumption.
Whether database/02_AlertServiceDb_Migrations.sql must be updated is unspecified.
unresolved_questions: Should AlertResponse.Tags be a string collection or tag DTO objects?
Should POST be idempotent for already-assigned tags, or return a conflict?
Should tag storage preserve submitted casing while comparisons remain case-insensitive?
Does DELETE match tag values case-insensitively?
Must the standalone SQL migration script be updated alongside the EF migration?
